PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-10-16
40F, general wellness examination.

S:
Patient presents for her yearly wellness visit. She reports feeling generally well overall. Over the past two months she has had occasional wheezing and chest tightness after brisk walking in cold air, easing within a few minutes of rest. Patient denies depression. She works as a graphic designer, mostly seated, and walks on weekends. Appetite is good; diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. Sleep is adequate. Lives with her partner. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 118/74, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 158 lb, BMI 25.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: nasal mucosa normal, oropharynx clear.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally at rest today.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema.
Psych: pleasant, normal affect, linear thought process.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.0%, basic metabolic panel within normal limits, lipid panel within goal.

A/P:
1. Possible mild intermittent asthma; will trial albuterol. Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs before exertion or as needed for wheezing. Inhaler technique reviewed. Spirometry ordered. Advised keeping a symptom diary for the next month.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular brisk walks on weekdays. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; discussed age-appropriate preventive care and immunizations. Influenza vaccine offered today.

Return in 6 weeks to review spirometry and the symptom diary, sooner if breathing worsens.
